8195.t: Uncertain. Commonly connected with Latin foedus (“ugly”).

8174.t: Perhaps from Ancient Greek πυραμός (pūramós) + -ίς (-ĭ́s), from πυρός (pūrós, “wheat”) + ἀμάω (amáō, “to reap”), or from Egyptian pr-m-ws (“height of a pyramid”), from pr (“(one that) comes forth”) + m (“from”) + ws (“height”).

8185.t: From the o-grade of πείρω (peírō, “to pierce, to run through”).

8199.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pótis, from Proto-Indo-European *pótis. Cognates include Albanian pata, Latin potis and Sanskrit पति॑ (páti).

8190.t: According to Beekes, from Proto-Indo-European *pélmn̥, from *pel- (“to cover, wrap; skin, hide; cloth”) and cognate with Proto-Germanic *felmô (“covering, skin”) (whence English film).

8165.t: From Proto-Indo-European *preh₃i, from *pró (“toward, leading to”). See also πρωΐ (prōĭ̈́, “morning”).

8189.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pélas, from Proto-Indo-European *pélh₂-s, from *pelh₂- (“to approach”).

8157.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *pr̥so- (“leek”), and connected with Latin porrum (“leek”) and Albanian presh.

8197.t: From Proto-Hellenic *póiwā, from Proto-Indo-European *póyH-weh₂, from *peyH-. Cognate with Lithuanian pieva (“meadow”).

8184.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰedʰ- (“to request, pray, ask for”). Cognate with English bid (“to invite, command”), Sanskrit गाध (gādha, “desire, cupidity”).

8192.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pékʷonts (“cooking, ripening”); related to πέσσω (péssō, “to soften, ripen”).

8196.t: Like many Greek words for pottery, most likely of Pre-Greek origin, as evidenced by the irregular variations between: * δ ~ θ (d ~ th), the former as in e.g. πίδος (pídos) * π ~ φ (p ~ ph), as in the derived terms πιθάκνη (pitháknē) ~ φιδάκνη (phidáknē)…

8166.t: According to Beekes, from a substrate root common to Proto-Slavic *brinъ (“larch”).

8164.t: In view of the close resemblance to Etruscan 𐌐𐌖𐌓𐌈𐌍𐌄 (purθne, “title of an official”), this word probably belongs to the Anatolian-Aegean stratum of social designations (compare ἄναξ (ánax), βασιλεύς (basileús) and τύραννος (túrannos)); attested with a…

8111.t: From προσ- (pros-) + μείγνυμι (meígnūmĭ), alternative form of μίγνυμι (mī́gnūmĭ).
